summary: gate.git-boundary.07 (standards pass): the bound test proves neither Then step of the failure path. Its staleness half is vacuous: the non-UTF-8 commit adds src/\xff.rs and leaves the declared surface src/main.rs untouched, so a lossy read of the diff would also report no stale-evidence and the assertion passes either way; the case that separates 'no answer' from 'clean' (one commit that changes the surface and adds the bad name) is only in the unbound canon-gate unit test staleness::tests::a_name_that_is_not_utf8_leaves_the_surface_query_unanswered_and_the_evidence_not_stale. The brief's 'the risk approval gives a violation' is not exercised at all: the CLI test only checks that approval-payload refuses; the violation is proved by the unbound risk::tests::a_commit_that_changed_a_name_that_is_not_utf8_closes_the_risk_check_as_an_unknown_analysis. I ran both unit tests and a black-box probe (one commit changing src/a.rs and adding a name with byte 0xff, surface src/a.rs: gate check clean, no stale-evidence) and the behaviour holds; the evidence bound to .07 does not show it. Fix: make the CLI test change the surface in the same commit and bind the two unit tests (or name them gate_git_boundary_07_*). Blast radius: .07 is the only scenario of the F2 failure path; the same weak setup lets a regression to lossy decoding pass CI.
